intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous rusted shipwreck make this an unforgettable experience. Boat tours typically depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and include stops at the Blue Caves.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Interact with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions and ingredients that have been staples for centuries.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach on Crete, famous for its unique pinkish-white sand caused by crushed coral and shells. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons to reach the small island of Elafonissi. Snorkel in the warm Mediterranean waters and relax on one of Europe's most beautiful and exotic-looking beaches.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna and learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan bruschetta), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades (honey donuts). Visit a local olive oil producer beforehand to understand the foundation of Greek cuisine. Enjoy your creations with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon and evening at Myrtos Beach on Kefalonia, consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in the Mediterranean. The dramatic contrast of the deep blue Ionian Sea against the white pebble beach and lush green cliffs is stunning. Stay for sunset when the sky turns golden over the water — a truly magical and free experience.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 (budget-friendly options) to reach your transfer point toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick souvlaki wrap or gyros from a kiosk near the airport or bus station (€3–5) before or during transfer

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros handy for bus fare (€6 for X95 or €10 for Metro to city center). Pre-book your onward transfer to the resort if it requires a ferry or regional bus. Confirm hotel check-in procedure for late arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, explore the immediate beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a slow morning stroll along the shoreline, get your bearings, and locate the nearest local shops, bakeries, and bus stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach (walking distance or short local bus ride). Swim in the warm June sea, relax on the sand, and soak up the hot sunny weather. Bring water and sunscreen — temperatures reach 29°C.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the nearest village or town center for a casual evening. Browse the waterfront promenade, watch the sunset, and settle into the holiday pace.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita (spinach pie) from a local bakery — a classic Greek budget breakfast for €1.50–2.50
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a mini-market (fruit, bread, olives, local cheese) and enjoy a picnic on the beach — budget €4–6
meals.dinner: Find a local taverna away from the tourist strip. Order a Greek salad (€5), grilled sardines or calamari (€7–9), and a carafe of house wine (€4–6). Total: ~€16–20

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to help you recover from the late arrival. Use the afternoon to orient yourself, ask hotel staff about free or cheap local beaches, and pick up a local SIM card if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby archaeological site or historic village within easy reach of the resort. Explore on foot or by local bus. Greece is rich in free or low-cost ancient ruins — many open from 8:00 AM and are best visited before midday heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for swimming during the warmest part of the day. Try snorkeling in the clear, warm June waters — bring your own gear or rent cheaply from a beach kiosk (€5–8). Look for rocky coves near the resort for better marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor cultural event, community square gathering, or simply enjoy the lively evening atmosphere (volta) as locals stroll the promenade after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café or mini-market — €2–3
meals.lunch: Order a gyros pita wrap with tzatziki from a local fast-food souvlaki shop — €2.50–3.50
meals.dinner: Try a mezedes (small plates) dinner at a budget taverna. Share dishes like taramasalata, dolmades, feta, and grilled bread. Budget €12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check opening hours for any archaeological sites in advance. Many Greek museums and sites offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early local bus or ferry to a nearby town or island port for a half-day exploration. Visit the local fish market or farmers' market if one is running — a fantastic way to see authentic Greek daily life and pick up cheap fresh produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a quieter, less-touristy beach nearby — ask locals for recommendations. Spend the afternoon swimming, reading, and relaxing. June's warm sea (around 23–24°C) makes extended swimming very comfortable.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. Cook a simple meal in the room if facilities allow, or pick up fresh ingredients from the market to save money.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor — €0.50–1.00, plus a Greek coffee (€1.50)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at the port — grilled fish of the day with bread and salad at a dockside taverna. Budget €10–14
meals.dinner: Self-catered or budget souvlaki shop — olives, local cheese, tomatoes, and bread from the market for €5–7

day_by_day.notes: Local buses in Greece are very affordable (€1.80–4 per ride). Ask the hotel for the nearest KTEL bus station. Ferry trips to nearby islands can be €5–15 each way depending on proximity.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — arrive early to claim a good spot before crowds build. Try a different beach section today, exploring further along the coastline on foot. Look for natural shade from rocks or trees to avoid buying expensive sunbed rentals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local monastery or Byzantine church in the area — typically free to enter and offering stunning architecture and peaceful grounds. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.evening: Join the Greek evening ritual: a leisurely dinner starting no earlier than 9:00 PM at a family-run taverna. This is when locals eat and the atmosphere is most authentic.

meals.breakfast: Café frappé (iced Greek coffee, €2) and a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry, €2–3) at a local café
meals.lunch: Horiatiki (traditional Greek salad) with crusty bread and olives at a beachside café — €6–8
meals.dinner: Family taverna dinner: moussaka or pastitsio (baked pasta dish) with a side salad and local beer. Budget €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Avoid sunbed rental fees (€5–15/day) by bringing your own towel and finding a free spot on the beach. Public beaches in Greece are legally free to access.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer day trip to a nearby island or coastal town by ferry or local bus. Depart early (7–8 AM) to maximize time. Research the most budget-friendly ferry route from the nearest port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination: walk through its main village, visit a hilltop viewpoint, and swim at one of its beaches. Smaller islands often have crystal-clear water and fewer crowds than main tourist hubs.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry or bus back to the resort area by early evening. Rest and enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Pack a simple breakfast from the mini-market before departure — fruit, bread, and juice for €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus or calamari at a portside taverna on the day-trip island — €8–12
meals.dinner: Simple dinner near the hotel: souvlaki plate with fries, tzatziki, and pita — €8–11

day_by_day.notes: Book return ferry tickets in advance during June as boats can fill up. Bring cash as smaller island vendors may not accept cards. Carry water and sunscreen for the full day out.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in, enjoy the hotel's beachfront location, and take a long, slow morning swim. June 21st is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year, giving you maximum daylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area on foot at a relaxed pace. Visit a local market, browse small shops, and pick up any souvenirs — look for locally made honey, olive oil, or ceramics rather than mass-produced tourist items.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset watching from a scenic coastal point near the hotel. This is the longest evening of the year — enjoy the extended golden hour and late sunset (around 8:45–9:00 PM in Greece in June).

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel café or a nearby spot: eggs, olives, feta, tomatoes, and bread — €5–8
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh juice and a cheese or ham toastie (tost) from a local café — €4–6
meals.dinner: Celebrate the solstice with a slightly more indulgent taverna meal: fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, tzatziki, and local wine. Budget €20–25 as a treat

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a great midpoint rest day. Use the afternoon to do laundry, plan the second week, and recharge. Many laundromats in Greek tourist areas charge €8–12 for a wash-and-dry service.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike or coastal walk to a nearby headland, cliff viewpoint, or nature trail. Starting before 8:30 AM means cooler temperatures and stunning morning light for photos. Bring water and wear sturdy sandals or trainers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a secluded cove or beach discovered during the morning walk. Pack a picnic lunch and enjoy a private-feeling beach experience away from the main tourist areas.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local ouzeri (traditional Greek bar) for ouzo or tsipouro with complimentary mezedes snacks — a very affordable and authentic Greek social experience.

meals.breakfast: Early energy-boosting breakfast: a honey and sesame bar (pasteli), banana, and Greek coffee from a kiosk — €2–3
meals.lunch: Picnic on the secluded beach: fresh bread, local olives, cherry tomatoes, hard-boiled eggs, and feta from the mini-market — €5–7
meals.dinner: Ouzeri dinner: order a carafe of ouzo (€4–6) and share 3–4 mezedes plates (€3–5 each). Total: €15–20

day_by_day.notes: At an ouzeri, it is traditional to receive small complimentary snacks with your drinks. Ouzo is an acquired taste — try it diluted with cold water as locals do. Always eat while drinking ouzo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fishing village within reach of the resort. Watch the fishermen return with their morning catch, explore the small harbor, and browse any dockside stalls. This is a wonderful window into traditional Greek coastal life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at the main resort beach. Try a free water activity: body surfing, snorkeling, or simply floating in the warm sea. If the hotel offers free or included watersports, take advantage today.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife area on a budget. Many Greek bars offer happy hour deals (€2–4 cocktails) from 6–8 PM. Enjoy the warm evening air at an outdoor bar or café.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fish breakfast at the fishing village: grilled sardines or fried anchovies with bread and lemon — €5–7 at a dockside café
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch: a cold Greek beer (€2–3) and a plate of fried zucchini balls (kolokythokeftedes) or cheese saganaki — €6–9
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly psarotaverna (fish taverna): order the catch of the day (priced by weight — ask first), with salad and bread. Budget €14–18

day_by_day.notes: When ordering fish by weight at a taverna, always confirm the price per kilo before ordering to avoid bill shock. A portion of 300–400g is usually sufficient for one person.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural morning: visit a local museum (archaeological, folk, or maritime) in the nearest town. Many regional Greek museums charge only €2–6 entry and are uncrowded — a far more authentic experience than major city museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a long swim and relaxation session. Bring a book, journal, or simply enjoy the view. The sea in late June is at its most inviting.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking experience: visit a local supermarket (AB Vassilopoulos, Lidl, or Sklavenitis are common budget-friendly chains) and buy ingredients to prepare a simple Greek meal. Many Greek accommodations have kitchen access.

meals.breakfast: Loukoumades (Greek honey donuts) from a local street stall — a portion for €3–4
meals.lunch: Museum café or nearby bakery sandwich — budget €4–6
meals.dinner: Self-cooked Greek feast: spaghetti with tomato and feta, Greek salad, and local bread. Ingredients from supermarket: €8–10 for two people

day_by_day.notes: Lidl and other discount supermarkets in Greece stock excellent local products (olive oil, olives, cheese, wine) at very low prices — great for self-catering and picking up food gifts to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day begins early. Explore a different beach along the coast — rent a bicycle (€5–10/day) or take a local bus to reach a beach 5–15 km away that you haven't visited yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the beach day. If the new beach has a beach bar, enjoy one affordable drink while people-watching. Try paddleboarding or kayaking if available at a reasonable rental rate (€8–12/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a final stroll through your favorite local spots. Pick up any last-minute local food souvenirs: honey, oregano, olive oil, or local wine.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt parfait with local honey and granola from a café — €3–5
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch: dakos (Cretan rusk salad with tomato and feta) and a cold Mythos beer — €7–10
meals.dinner: Revisit your favorite taverna from the trip for a nostalgic last-big-dinner. Order your favorite dishes from the week — budget €15–20

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental is one of the best budget ways to explore the Greek coast. Many rental shops offer half-day rates. Always wear sunscreen and carry water when cycling in 29°C heat.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning — take one last long swim in the warm Greek sea. Pack a bag and spend the morning at the beachfront, reflecting on the trip. Take photos of the view from the hotel beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (if checkout is at midday) or request a late checkout. Spend the early afternoon doing any final local exploration, buying last-minute items, or simply sitting at a waterfront café with a cold drink.
day_by_day.evening: Begin travel toward the airport or onward destination. If flying the next day, travel to Athens or the nearest airport city and find budget accommodation near the airport (hostels from €20–30/night).

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast: fresh orange juice, a warm tiropita, and a Greek coffee at your favorite local spot — €4–6
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch: a mezedes spread to share — tzatziki, hummus, olives, pita, and feta — €10–14
meals.dinner: Airport area or city dinner: souvlaki wrap or a simple taverna meal near your overnight stop — €8–12

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is early on Day 13, consider staying near the airport the night before to avoid a stressful early-morning journey. Athens airport has 24-hour facilities including cafés and currency exchange.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece. If time allows before airport transfer, enjoy one last Greek coffee and a pastry at an airport café or a nearby spot. Do a final check of all belongings, passport, and boarding pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Greece. Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Clear security and enjoy duty-free browsing (Greek olive oil and honey make excellent affordable gifts).
day_by_day.evening: In transit or arrived home. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, fresh seafood, warm hospitality, and sun-drenched coastline.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek coffee and a koulouri or pastry at the airport or nearby café — €3–5
meals.lunch: Airport meal or packed snacks from the supermarket — budget €6–10
meals.dinner: On the plane or upon arrival home

day_by_day.notes: Greece imposes no departure tax separately — it is included in your flight ticket. Duty-free allowances apply for EU and non-EU travelers. Keep your receipts for any VAT refund claims if eligible. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival — expect to spend around €15–20

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer with the resort to avoid delays at night. Keep snacks handy for the journey. Rest well — your Greek adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy a stroll along the beachfront promenade directly in front of Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time and take in the stunning coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's private beach. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (approx. €10–15), swim in the crystal-clear water, and explore the shoreline. Visit a nearby local beach kiosk to try your first Greek freddo espresso.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest village or harbour on foot. Browse small shops and get your bearings. Watch the golden-hour sunset over the sea from a waterfront spot.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or approx. €12–18. Try Greek yogurt with honey and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Casual beachside taverna near the resort — try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and fresh pita bread. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant in the nearby village — order fresh catch of the day, tzatziki, and a glass of local white wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation and recovery day. Don't over-plan — let yourself ease into the pace of Greek island life. Sunscreen is essential from day one; UV index will be high.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a morning swim before the beaches get busy — water temperature is ideal in June. Then join a local guided walking tour of the nearest historic town or village, exploring traditional whitewashed architecture, churches, and hidden alleyways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local open-air market or agora to browse fresh produce, olives, cheeses, and handmade goods. Pick up some local snacks like sesame-coated koulouri bread rings and dried figs. Head to a quieter, less-touristy beach recommended by locals for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up, then head out for a relaxed evening at a traditional Greek taverna. Enjoy a long, leisurely dinner in true Greek fashion.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with thyme honey and walnuts at a local café — approx. €6–10.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch using market finds — olives, local cheese, bread, tomatoes, and fruit. Budget €10–15 total.
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner — moussaka, slow-roasted lamb, horiatiki salad, and house wine or local beer. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Markets typically open early and wind down by early afternoon — aim to arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM. Bring a small tote bag for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip or ferry excursion to a nearby secluded cove or small uninhabited islet. These short trips (1–2 hours) are widely available from local harbours and offer snorkelling in pristine, clear water. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the islet or return to a scenic beach along the coastline. Snorkel among sea grass and rocky outcrops, spot sea urchins and small fish, and soak up the sun on a quieter stretch of sand.
day_by_day.evening: Back on the main island, visit a local ouzeri (traditional Greek bar) for an aperitif experience — order ouzo or tsipouro with complimentary small mezedes plates.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — eggs, fresh bread, local honey, and fruit. Approx. €12–18 if not included.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch to bring on the boat — sandwiches, fruit, and water. Alternatively, many boat trips stop at a taverna on a small island. Budget €15–20.
meals.dinner: Seafood-focused restaurant near the harbour — grilled sea bass, shrimp saganaki, and fresh bread. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book boat excursions the evening before as they fill up quickly in June. Apply waterproof sunscreen before boarding. Bring a hat and light cover-up for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local archaeological site or hilltop ancient ruins in the region — Greece is dotted with accessible ancient temples, fortresses, and Byzantine churches even outside of major tourist hubs. Hire a local guide for context and stories (approx. €15–25).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off at one of the area's most famous and scenic beaches. Arrive by early afternoon before peak heat. Swim, relax, and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery. Many scenic beaches have beach bars where you can order a cold drink and a light snack.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the main town's pedestrian streets as locals come out for their evening volta (traditional evening promenade). Browse boutique shops for locally made ceramics, olive oil products, and jewellery.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach and feta pie) and a Greek coffee at a local bakery — approx. €5–8.
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — club sandwich, Greek salad, fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Rooftop or terrace restaurant with sea views — try lamb chops (paidakia), roasted vegetables, and local red wine. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the archaeological site — paths can be uneven and rocky. Carry water, especially during the midday heat around 29°C.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class with a local Greek chef or home cook. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as dolmades (stuffed vine leaves), tzatziki, and spanakopita using fresh, seasonal ingredients. Classes typically run 2–3 hours and include a sit-down meal of what you cooked.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or small family-run winery for a guided tasting experience. Learn about traditional olive oil production or sample regional wines with a knowledgeable host. This is a wonderful way to connect with Greek agricultural heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy the pool or beachfront, watch the sunset, and dine at the resort's own restaurant for a change of pace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — the meal you prepare together. Budget €45–65 per person for the class including lunch.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — fresh grilled fish, seasonal vegetables, and a glass of wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance as spots are limited. Winery and olive grove visits are often free or low-cost (€10–20) and deeply rewarding for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or coastal town accessible by ferry or local boat. Spend the morning on the ferry enjoying sea views and arriving to explore a new destination — a charming fishing village, a dramatic cliff-top town, or a quieter, less-visited island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination on foot — wander narrow lanes, visit a local church or museum, and find a beautiful beach or viewpoint. Have lunch at a local taverna favoured by residents rather than tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry in the late afternoon or early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort, reflecting on the day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departing — yogurt, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Local taverna at the day-trip destination — try whatever the daily special is (the 'mageirefta' or home-cooked dishes). Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Small neighbourhood restaurant near the resort — stuffed peppers, grilled chicken souvlaki, and house salad. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance and book return tickets. Carry cash as smaller island tavernas may not accept cards. Wear comfortable shoes for exploring uneven cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in, enjoy breakfast slowly, and spend time reading or journalling on your resort balcony or the beach. This is a deliberate rest day mid-trip to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter, quad bike, or small car (approx. €25–50/day) and explore the island or coastal region independently. Drive along scenic coastal roads, stop at viewpoints, discover hidden beaches, and visit a traditional mountain village inland.
day_by_day.evening: Find a clifftop or elevated spot to watch the sunset — one of Greece's most iconic experiences. Many villages have designated sunset viewing areas with small bars or cafés.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy every bite.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside souvlaki stand or village kafeneion (traditional café) during your drive — gyros wrap or grilled meat skewers with pita. Budget €8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner at a clifftop taverna — fresh mussels, grilled calamari, and local wine while watching the colours fade over the Aegean. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter or quad, ensure you have a valid driving licence and wear a helmet. Fuel up before heading into rural areas. Download an offline map in case of poor mobile coverage.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a traditional Greek monastery or Byzantine church in the region — many are perched on hilltops or cliffside locations with breathtaking views. These are free or request a small donation. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a beach known for its natural beauty — perhaps one with dramatic rock formations, a sea cave, or exceptionally clear turquoise water. Spend several hours swimming, snorkelling, and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local food tour or street food walk in the nearest town — sample loukoumades (honey-drenched doughnuts), grilled corn, cheese pies, and local sweets from market stalls and small shops.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and freddo cappuccino at a local bakery — approx. €5–8.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — simple grilled fish, village salad, and cold Mythos beer. Budget €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Street food tour or self-guided street food evening — budget €20–30 per person for multiple small tastings.

day_by_day.notes: Carry a light scarf or sarong to cover up when visiting religious sites. Most monasteries have visiting hours — typically open in the morning and early evening, closed during midday.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning kayaking or paddleboarding session along the coastline — many resorts and beach operators offer rentals (€15–25/hour) or guided tours. The calm morning sea is perfect for paddling into sea caves and along cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fish market or fishing harbour and watch the afternoon catch come in. Chat with fishermen if possible and observe the lively scene. Then spend time at a nearby beach or chill at a beach bar with a book.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live Greek music performance at a local bar, taverna, or cultural venue. Traditional Greek music (laïká or rebetiko) performed live is an authentic and memorable experience.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before kayaking — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee at the resort.
meals.lunch: Harbour-side lunch — fresh grilled sardines, fava bean dip, and crusty bread at a no-frills fisherman's taverna. Budget €15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Taverna with live music — mezedes sharing plates including saganaki (fried cheese), meatballs in tomato sauce, and stuffed mushrooms. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayaking session the day before. For live music venues, ask hotel staff for recommendations — they'll know the authentic spots versus tourist-oriented shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local museum — a folklore museum, maritime museum, or archaeological museum depending on what's available in the region. These smaller regional museums offer fascinating insight into local history and culture, often with English signage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a long, luxurious afternoon at the beach — your last full beach day, so make the most of it. Swim, float, and soak up the Aegean sun. Try a water sport you haven't done yet — jet skiing, parasailing, or banana boat riding.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner — a mid-range restaurant with a refined menu and beautiful ambience to celebrate a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — full spread with eggs, cold cuts, cheese, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Beach club or upscale beach bar — fresh salads, grilled prawns, and a refreshing cocktail. Budget €25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Greek restaurant — slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, grilled lobster pasta, and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini. Budget €40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Museum admission is typically €4–10. Water sports are priced per activity — budget €20–50 depending on what you choose. This is a great day to buy any remaining souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim in the Aegean — savour every moment in the warm, clear water. Take a long walk along the beach to collect memories (and maybe a few smooth sea stones as keepsakes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any spots you may have missed or return to a favourite place from earlier in the trip. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping — local honey, olive oil, herbs, ceramic tiles, and evil eye charms make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favourite restaurant discovered during the trip, or try one final new spot recommended by locals. Toast to an incredible 13-day Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — enjoy it fully as one of your last mornings.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café — a mezedes plate, fresh bread, and a cold drink. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — return to your favourite taverna or try a highly recommended spot. Order generously and share plates. Budget €30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing in the evening. Keep travel documents, chargers, and essentials in your carry-on. Confirm any departure transfers or taxi bookings for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a last Greek coffee and pastry at a local café before checking out. Take a final stroll along the waterfront and breathe in the sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and transfer to the airport or ferry port for your onward journey. Allow plenty of time for travel and check-in procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry wonderful memories of beaches, food, sunsets, and the warmth of Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a local café — koulouri, tiropita, and a strong Greek coffee. Approx. €6–10.
meals.lunch: Light airport or port meal — or pick up snacks from a local bakery before departing. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Store luggage at the hotel if your transfer is later in the day. Greece will be waiting for your return!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous rusted shipwreck make this an unforgettable experience. Boat tours typically depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and include stops at the Blue Caves.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Interact with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions and ingredients that have been staples for centuries.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach on Crete, famous for its unique pinkish-white sand caused by crushed coral and shells. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons to reach the small island of Elafonissi. Snorkel in the warm Mediterranean waters and relax on one of Europe's most beautiful and exotic-looking beaches.

experiences.name: Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon and evening at Myrtos Beach on Kefalonia, consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in the Mediterranean. The dramatic contrast of the deep blue Ionian Sea against the white pebble beach and lush green cliffs is stunning. Stay for sunset when the sky turns golden over the water — a truly magical and free experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged Mercedes V-Class) whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity, and unwind with a nightcap at the resort's rooftop bar overlooking the sea.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Late-night light supper at the resort's 24-hour lounge — charcuterie board, local cheeses, olives, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. No sightseeing scheduled. Confirm private transfer with resort concierge before departure. Resort check-in is available 24/7.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle orientation stroll along the beachfront promenade to acclimate to the surroundings. Spend time at the resort's private beach — crystal-clear warm Aegean water, sun loungers, and complimentary water sports equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment at the resort's thalassotherapy spa — choose from a Greek olive oil massage or a sea-mineral body wrap. Afterward, relax by the infinity pool with a fresh fruit cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's terrace, then a reservation at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a multi-course Greek tasting menu paired with curated wines.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant — fresh pastries, local honey, Cretan graviera cheese, smoked salmon, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch at the resort — grilled octopus, Greek salad with barrel-aged feta, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: 5-course tasting menu featuring sea bass carpaccio, lobster bisque, lamb kleftiko, local cheese selection, and baklava soufflé — paired with sommelier-selected Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Treat Day 2 as a recovery and resort orientation day. Book spa treatments in advance through the concierge. Dress code for the signature restaurant is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour: Join an exclusive private guided food tour of the legendary Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market). Sample cured meats, fresh cheeses, marinated olives, spiced nuts, and local street food. Learn about Greek culinary traditions directly from market vendors and your expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, explore the historic Monastiraki and Plaka neighbourhoods on foot. Visit a premium olive oil boutique and a curated Greek wine shop for tastings and bespoke purchases to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner reservation at a renowned Athens restaurant in the Kolonaki district — rooftop views of the Acropolis, elevated modern Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh fruits, yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, and espresso
meals.lunch: Immersive tasting lunch woven into the Athens Central Market Food Tour — mezedes spread including taramosalata, spanakopita, loukoumades (honey doughnuts), and fresh-grilled souvlaki at a legendary market taverna
meals.dinner: Upscale Athens rooftop restaurant: slow-roasted lamb shoulder with lemon potatoes, grilled whole sea bream, and a selection of Greek mezedes — accompanied by a bottle of Naoussa Xinomavro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Private car transfer to and from Athens recommended (approx. 30–45 min depending on resort location). Book the food tour and dinner well in advance. Comfortable walking shoes advised for the market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yacht charter departing from the nearest marina. Sail along the coastline, stopping at secluded coves for snorkelling in pristine turquoise water. The yacht comes equipped with snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and a stocked refreshment bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht journey to a hidden sea cave or a remote beach accessible only by boat. Anchor for a swim and enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort's chef and served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Freshen up, then enjoy a private beachside dinner under the stars — a bespoke table set on the sand with torchlight and personalised service.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — Greek yogurt parfait, granola, seasonal fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-deck picnic: artisan bread, Santorini cherry tomatoes, local cheeses, cold cuts, marinated seafood, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner: whole grilled lobster, stuffed vine leaves, grilled halloumi, roasted vegetable medley, and a decadent chocolate and walnut dessert — paired with a premium sparkling Greek wine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm yacht charter at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Apply high-SPF sunscreen and bring a hat and light cover-up for the day at sea. Life jackets available on board.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Elafonissi Beach on Crete (if resort is Crete-based) or arrange a luxury seaplane/helicopter transfer for a seamless island-hopping experience. Arrive early to enjoy the famous pinkish-white sands before day-trippers arrive. Wade through the shallow lagoon and swim in the warm, glassy water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Elafonissi — hike the short nature trail through the dunes and juniper scrubland to reach quieter stretches of beach. Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol in a VIP beach section for the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a nearby seaside taverna recommended by the concierge — authentic Cretan cuisine in a charming setting.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — Cretan dakos (rusks with tomato and feta), soft-boiled eggs, fresh orange juice, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the best local restaurant near Elafonissi: fresh grilled fish of the day, Cretan horta (wild greens), and local bread with extra-virgin olive oil
meals.dinner: Traditional Cretan taverna dinner: slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi greens, fresh calamari, grilled sardines, and a carafe of local Cretan white wine followed by loukoumades with honey and cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is best visited early — aim to arrive by 9:00 AM. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the unique ecosystem. The beach has limited facilities so pack essentials. Book return transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a local Greek chef at a traditional farmhouse or luxury villa kitchen. Learn to prepare classic dishes — spanakopita, moussaka, fresh tzatziki, and a honey-walnut dessert — using locally sourced ingredients including herbs from the garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class, sit down to enjoy the meal you've prepared in a beautiful alfresco setting. Visit a nearby local olive grove or vineyard for a guided tour and premium tasting of estate olive oils and wines.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening at the resort. Sunset aperitivo on the terrace, followed by dinner at the resort's beachfront grill restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: full Greek spread — fresh figs, local honey, assorted pastries, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and a Nespresso or Greek frappe
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class, enjoyed alfresco with local wine and freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront grill: charcoal-grilled swordfish souvlaki, roasted red peppers stuffed with feta and herbs, Greek village salad, and a chilled bottle of Moscofilero white wine

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically last 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting a little messy. The concierge can arrange transport to the farmhouse. Olive grove tours usually include complimentary tasting samples.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to a significant local archaeological site or hilltop village near the resort. Explore narrow cobblestone streets, whitewashed churches, and artisan boutiques. Engage with a local historian guide for rich cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Take advantage of the resort's water sports offerings — try jet skiing, paddleboarding, or a guided kayak tour along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a clifftop bar with panoramic sea views. Dinner at an acclaimed local restaurant known for its creative take on traditional Greek recipes.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Greek yogurt with pistachio and pomegranate, avocado toast on sourdough, freshly squeezed juice, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming village taverna: lamb chops with roasted potatoes, stuffed tomatoes and peppers (gemista), and a glass of local red wine
meals.dinner: Award-winning local restaurant: tuna tartare with cucumber and dill, slow-braised pork belly with fig reduction, grilled prawns with lemon and herbs, and a baklava ice cream sandwich for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the village exploration. The clifftop bar is popular at sunset — arrive by 19:30 to secure a good table. Book the evening restaurant well in advance, especially on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit on Zakynthos: Depart early via a private luxury speedboat charter or helicopter transfer to Zakynthos. Arrive at the iconic Navagio Beach — sheer white limestone cliffs, the rusted shipwreck, and dazzling turquoise water — before the crowds. Swim and explore at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Zakynthos by private boat — visit the Blue Caves, where sunlight refracts through the water creating electric blue hues. Stop for a swim in a secluded cove and enjoy the on-board refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) before the return transfer, or enjoy a sunset dinner on the boat deck as you cruise back.

meals.breakfast: Light grab-and-go breakfast at the resort before early departure — energy bars, fresh fruit, and thermos coffee
meals.lunch: On-board gourmet picnic: fresh shrimp, smoked fish, artisan cheeses, olives, crusty bread, and chilled white wine served on deck at Navagio Bay
meals.dinner: Zakynthos Town fine-dining restaurant: pan-seared sea bass with capers and lemon butter, grilled octopus with fava purée, and a classic Greek dessert platter with local honey and walnuts

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat. Book the private charter well in advance. The beach can be crowded midday — arriving early is essential for a premium experience. Bring waterproof camera or GoPro for the Blue Caves.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort relaxation morning — lie in, then enjoy a private yoga or Pilates session on the beach at sunrise with the resort's wellness instructor. Follow with a refreshing dip in the sea and a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience preparation: arrange a private chauffeured transfer to Myrtos Beach on Kefalonia (if accessible from resort). Spend the afternoon at one of Greece's most spectacular beaches — dramatic white pebbles, impossibly blue water, and towering green cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the legendary Myrtos Beach sunset — the light turns the cliffs golden and the water a deep sapphire. Return to the resort for a late dinner at the resort's wine bar and lounge.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga resort breakfast: smoothie bowls, granola, poached eggs on sourdough, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch near Myrtos: fresh grilled fish, Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), and local beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort wine bar and lounge: grazing dinner of premium mezedes — truffle-infused taramosalata, wagyu beef skewers, grilled halloumi with watermelon and mint, and a curated Greek wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has limited shade — bring a parasol or rent one on arrival. The beach is pebbly so water shoes are recommended. The sunset here is extraordinary and worth timing your visit around (approximately 20:45–21:15 in June).

day_by_day.morning: Private deep-sea fishing charter departing at dawn. Try your hand at line fishing in the Ionian or Aegean Sea with an experienced local captain. The catch of the day can be taken back to the resort's chef for preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by midday. Hand your catch to the chef for a personalised 'catch-to-table' lunch experience. Spend the rest of the afternoon at the resort's beach club with cocktails and a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive wine and cheese pairing event at the resort — hosted by a sommelier specialising in Greek wines. Taste rare indigenous varieties such as Limnio, Robola, and Mavrodaphne paired with artisan Greek cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast before fishing departure — croissants, yogurt, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Catch-to-table lunch prepared by the resort chef: your fresh fish grilled whole with lemon, herbs, and olive oil, served with roasted vegetables and Greek salad
meals.dinner: Wine and cheese pairing event at the resort: 6 Greek wines matched with 6 artisan cheeses, accompanied by honey, quince paste, walnuts, and fresh bread — a true gastronomic journey through Greece's wine regions

day_by_day.notes: Fishing charter requires early wake-up (around 05:30). Motion sickness medication recommended if prone to seasickness. Inform the resort chef the evening before about the catch-to-table lunch so they can prepare accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided boat tour to a series of hidden sea caves and emerald lagoons along the coastline. Snorkel through underwater arches, spot colourful marine life, and explore grottos accessible only by small boat or swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious afternoon. Book a second spa session — try the 'Aegean Ritual': a full-body sea salt scrub, followed by a warm oil massage using Greek herbs and a facial with local honey and olive extract.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner at the resort's most exclusive restaurant — reserve the chef's table for a personalised 7-course tasting menu with wine pairings, celebrating the penultimate evening of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: eggs cooked to order, fresh fruit platter, Greek pastries, and a glass of fresh pomegranate juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat or at a waterside café: grilled calamari, fresh bread with taramasalata, and a cold Mythos beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Chef's table 7-course tasting menu: amuse-bouche of smoked eel on blini, sea urchin with lemon cream, seared scallop with saffron risotto, duck confit with fig and ouzo reduction, lamb rack with herb crust, Greek cheese trolley, and a honey-soaked loukoumades dessert with vanilla ice cream — paired with 7 premium Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table typically accommodates 2–6 guests and must be booked well in advance — ideally at check-in. This is the premium highlight dining experience of the trip. Smart elegant attire recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning beach walk at sunrise — a peaceful, reflective stroll along the resort's private stretch of coastline. Collect sea glass or simply soak in the last morning of warm Aegean air. Optional: one final swim in the crystal-clear sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan market or boutique for premium Greek souvenirs — hand-painted ceramics, pure Cretan olive oil, saffron from Kozani, local honey, and authentic Greek jewellery. Enjoy a final afternoon at the resort's infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest local restaurant in the nearest town — a celebratory meal to honour 13 days of extraordinary Greek experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: the full works — every favourite from the past 12 days, enjoyed slowly with great coffee and sea views
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beloved local spot near the market: souvlaki wraps, fresh lemonade, and loukoumades with honey
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant: seafood tower starter, grilled whole fish, roasted lamb, traditional dessert medley (galaktoboureko, baklava, kataifi), and a bottle of premium Greek sparkling wine to toast the journey

day_by_day.notes: Allow time for packing in the afternoon. Confirm departure logistics with the concierge — private transfer timing, luggage storage, and any last-minute requests. Leave a review or gratuity for exceptional resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort depending on departure time. Enjoy a last breakfast with sea views. Take a final dip in the Aegean if time allows. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — luggage handled by resort staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Arrive with ample time to enjoy the airport's premium lounge — shower, light refreshments, and duty-free browsing for any last Greek treasures.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with extraordinary memories of 13 days of beaches, flavours, sunsets, and Aegean magic. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and a perfect Greek coffee — savoured slowly with a view of the sea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a farewell souvlaki at a classic spot near the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or departure lounge dinner — treat yourself to a glass of Greek wine to extend the holiday spirit just a little longer

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 — request a late check-out (14:00 or later) if your transfer allows. Keep travel documents, passports, and any purchased artisan items in carry-on luggage. Confirm flight details the evening before departure.
